name: Christian Catholic Church in Zion

citations.excerpt: the name assumed by a religious organization founded at Zion City near Chicago, Illinois, U.S.A., in 1896, by John Alexander Dowie ( q.v. ).

facts.value: Faith healing and threefold immersion of believers.

citations.excerpt: Its members added to the usual tenets of Christianity a special belief in faith-healing, and laid much stress on united consecration services and the threefold immersion of believers.

facts.value: A community founded at Zion City near Chicago in 1896, with religious, educational and commercial departments. Dowie was deposed in 1906 after dissension among his followers.

citations.excerpt: After 1903 considerable dissension arose among Dowie’s followers: he was deposed in 1906
